profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary: Experienced in multidisciplinary fields of engineering - data software, embedded firmware and hardware. Cross-functional team leader and mentor. Currently focusing on payment data analytics.

positions.title: Technical Lead, Data Engineering
positions.description:
Developed an Airflow-based data pipeline running 15+ DAG jobs among multiple sources and destinations. Managed data transformations and continuous replication (< 2min lag) between databases and data warehouse.

Deployed  20+ real time dashboards showing live (30s refresh) performance metrics across 8 store locations for internal analytics. Responsible for building both the back-end data pipeline and the front-end dashboard.

Automated growth marketing engineering effort to filter and and issue 9 promotions via email and push notification. This is powered by a REST API microservice that surfaces 100K+ customer activity data using serverless AWS components

positions.title: Technical Lead, Data Engineering
positions.description:
Architected a data pipeline for uploading, storing, and visualizing real time (<5s lag) electric vehicle (EV) data based on a highly scalable and available serverless architecture

Researched lithium-ion battery management algorithms (cell balancing, state-of-charge, capacity, power limits, voltage prediction, thermal control) by analyzing 6+ years of datasets for EV battery management system (BMS)

Developed efficient, real-time algorithms in C for resource-constrained embedded microcontrollers and designed automated hardware-in-loop testbed to simulate and validate algorithms

positions.title: Technical Staff, Hardware Engineering
positions.description:
Built 5+ battery management boards to control and monitor essential battery pack parameters such as current, voltage, and temperature. Managed 3 generations of BMS, eBMS, BCM, MCB, VSB, TCB boards.

Designed embedded systems with microcontrollers, power regulators, filters, ADC, I2C, SPI, CAN for PCB schematics, layout, fabrication, and bring-up at 1-month development cycles.

positions.title: Electrical Engineer
positions.description:
Synexis Electrical, Silicon Systems Group

Integrated sensors (infrared camera, water leak sensor, power monitor) into Chemical-Mechanical Polisher (CMP)

Designed submodule interconnect harnesses and debugged OEM device issues (servo motor controller) for CMP

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Introductory Electronics (E40) and Circuits I (EE101A)

Taught introductory analog and digital circuit modeling and analysis along with other EE fundamentals

Managed weekly laboratory sessions, held office hours and administered exams for undergraduate EE students

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description:
Mobile Mac Hardware Group

Simulated power density profiles on MacBookPro PCB logic boards to identify voltage drops and current hotspots

Conducted general hardware characterization (ref. voltage checks) and debugging (boot sequence verification)

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) program

Modified a hard disk drive into a MATLAB-controlled inertial actuator for testing prototype MEMS accelerometers at Stanford MEMS laboratory

Conducted a finite element method (FEM) simulation of silicon networks for stretchable smart surface application at Stanford Organic Electronics Laboratory (SOEL)

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description: Engaged in market research, database management, and refurbished hardware testing.

honors.title: Samsung Scholarship Recipient
honors.description:
One of 25 Korean high school students from around the world to receive full financial support for 4 years of undergraduate education in the US.

Stretchable Silicon Wired Sensor Networks For Smart Materials

patents.title: Method and Apparatus for Selectively Heating Individual Battery Modules Within a Battery Pack
patents.description: A system and method are provided which, when the battery pack is at a low charge level, selectively heat the battery or battery module with the lowest voltage, thereby decreasing the internal resistance and mitigating the magnitude of the voltage drop of the affected battery/battery module. As a result, termination of the battery pack's discharge cycle is delayed and the driving range of the vehicle is increased, thereby giving the driver a little more time and driving range to reach a charging station.
